To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the relationship between changes of employment in Portuguese manufacturing and marginal intra-industry exports is according to smooth hypothesis, (b) the relationship between employment changes and changes of domestic consumption in Portuguese manufacturing is negative, (c) the relationship between growth in productivity and marginal intra-industrial trade is positive, (d) the relationship between productivity growth and changes in employment is positive,
marginal intra-industry trades have a negative impact on labor market adjustments in Portugal.
marginal intra-industry and marginal bilateral trade have negative effects on the amplitude of employment change in Portugal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of IIT on the labor market.
the relationship between labor market adjustments, IIT and market structure in Portugal over the period of 1995-2006.
the impact of intra industry trade and adjustment costs in labor market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
marginal intra-industry is a factor of adjustment costs in labor market, which means a negative impact on the labor market.

the Portuguese economy has experienced a significant amount of labor market adjustments under the impact of IIT, but these adjustments have been relatively small and slow, which may be a sign of the existence of high adjustment costs.
the labor market is more sensitive to changes in consumption than to changes in productivity and marginal intra-industry exchange.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the labor market adjustments are according to smooth adjustment theory in Portugal.
marginal intra-industry is a good indicator for employment changes.
the labor market adjustments according a smooth adjustment hypothesis are more important for the Portuguese economy than the labor market adjustments that are not according to smooth adjustment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
marginal intra-industry and intra-industry trade are not sufficient to generate employment changes.
marginal intra-industry is a relevant factor in explaining the amplitude of labor market adjustments.
the Portuguese economy has been characterized by a high level of intra-industry specialization, which has been a source of adjustment costs for the labor market.
